tagline: Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue.
mission: To increase the GDP of the internet by building the most powerful and flexible financial infrastructure for businesses of every size, from first transaction to billionth.
summary: Stripe is the backbone of global commerce — a developer-first, enterprise-grade payments and financial platform that lets businesses accept payments, build billing models, issue cards, move money globally, and embed financial services into any product. It combines technical depth with elegant simplicity, trusted by startups and 50% of Fortune 100 companies alike.
target_audience: Founders, CTOs, product managers, and finance leaders at high-growth startups, scaling SaaS companies, marketplaces, and enterprise organizations who need reliable, programmable financial infrastructure without operational friction.

personas.name: The Ambitious Founder
personas.description: A 28-35 year old tech entrepreneur launching or scaling a SaaS or marketplace product, obsessed with shipping fast and not getting bogged down by payment complexity. They want infrastructure that just works so they can focus on growth.

personas.name: The Enterprise Architect
personas.description: A senior engineering or product leader at a Fortune 500 company, mid-40s, tasked with modernizing legacy payment systems. They need proven reliability, global scale, and a platform that integrates cleanly into complex existing stacks.

personas.name: The Global Commerce Operator
personas.description: A 30-40 year old head of payments or revenue operations at a fast-scaling e-commerce or platform business, managing multi-currency transactions and international expansion. They care about conversion rates, uptime, and borderless money movement.

personas.name: The Developer Builder
personas.description: A 22-32 year old full-stack engineer who is the internal champion for Stripe adoption, energized by clean APIs and excellent documentation. They evaluate tools by how quickly they can ship a proof of concept and how far the platform can scale.

selling_points: 135+ currencies and payment methods supported globally
$1.9 trillion in payments volume processed in 2025
200M+ active subscriptions managed on Stripe Billing
Flexible billing models: subscriptions, usage-based, one-time, and custom
Embedded payments for platforms and marketplaces
Card issuing program creation built into the platform
Stablecoin and crypto-enabled borderless money movement
Agentic commerce monetization for AI-driven business models
Unified online and in-person payment infrastructure
Personalized product recommendations based on business type
emotional_motivations: Confidence that payments will never be the reason growth stalls
Pride in building on infrastructure trusted by the world's best companies
Relief from the complexity and anxiety of managing global money movement
Ambition to scale without limits — from first transaction to billionth
Control over revenue models without engineering constraints
Trust in a platform with proven, measurable reliability
voice_notes: Write with technical authority but never jargon for jargon's sake. Lead with scale and capability, then ground it in concrete numbers and real outcomes. Sentences should be tight and declarative — no fluff, no hype. Use active voice. Speak to builders and decision-makers as peers. Avoid superlatives unless backed by data. The tone is calm confidence: Stripe doesn't need to shout because the numbers speak. When writing CTAs, be direct and action-oriented ('Start building', 'See the docs', 'Talk to sales').
casting_notes: Cast real-looking founders, engineers, and operators aged 25-45 — diverse in background, sharp in energy, working in real environments: modern open offices, home setups with multiple monitors, co-working spaces, or retail floors. Avoid overly polished or stock-photo aesthetics. Subjects should look like they're actually building something, not posing. Wardrobe: smart-casual, functional. Energy: focused, purposeful, quietly excited — not loud or salesy. For enterprise spots, include team settings and boardroom-adjacent contexts that signal scale without feeling stiff.
rules: DO: Use real metrics and proof points in copy whenever possible. DO: Reflect the full spectrum of business sizes — from solo founders to Fortune 100. DO: Pair technical capability with business outcome language. DO: Use the deep indigo (#533afd) as the dominant brand signal in visuals. DO: Show the product (dashboard, API, checkout) in context — not as abstract UI. DO: Maintain visual cleanliness — generous whitespace, structured layouts. DON'T: Use generic 'payments made easy' language — Stripe is infrastructure, not a widget. DON'T: Overpromise or use unsubstantiated superlatives. DON'T: Show chaotic, cluttered, or low-fidelity creative — quality signals trust. DON'T: Use humor that undermines credibility — wit is fine, slapstick is not. DON'T: Ignore developer and technical audiences in favor of pure business messaging. DON'T: Use competitor names or comparative claims. DON'T: Depict payment failure, fraud, or downtime scenarios — reinforce reliability always.
